These compounds, in turn, target the same downstream entity, the Proteasome subunit beta type-5. The high scores across all three paths indicate a consistent and significant relationship, likely due to the shared biological role of the target entity in cellular processes. The evidence suggests that glycopyrrolate may exert its effects through a mechanism that involves the activation of cGMP 3',5'-cyclic phosphodiesterase subunit gamma, which in turn activates the Proteasome subunit beta type-5. This indirect pathway highlights the importance of the target entity in mediating the drug's effects, though the exact mechanism remains to be fully elucidated.
